newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: ADB promises $380 million for Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: ADB promises $380 million for Cambodia.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday announced plans to provide $380 million in loans through the year 2000 for Cambodia's economy, which it said was growing at a robust rate.

The loans would likely comprise $90 million in 1997, $110 million in 1998, $90 million in 1999 and $90 million in 2000 to support economic growth, policy reform, human resource development and natural resources conservation, an ADB statement said.
Projects receiving loan money included programmes for infrastructure, agriculture and water, social welfare, finance, industry and the environment.
With a robust 6.5 percent growth in the gross domestic product in 1996 and stable inflation of about nine percent, Cambodia's economy had performed well, ADB officials said.
The government has reported 1996 inflation at closer to seven percent than nine percent.

"It is healthy enough, it's not sick. Cambodia has...good development potential because it is located within the buoyant economies of Southeast Asia, provided all the ingredients work together," said the Cambodia's bank representative, Suos Someth.
The ADB said economic performance had been linked to investment, market-oriented reforms and avoidance of bank financing for fiscal deficits.
War-scarred Cambodia has made some gains since opening its economy in the early 1990s but it remains one of Asia's poorest nations, with annual per capita income at under $300.
